title: JAMB Commercial
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public JAMB UTME commercial-subject syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: The market women had complained for months that the road to the farm was impassable, but nothing was done until a loaded lorry sank in the mud and blocked the only route to town. Within a week the council sent graders to repair it. Why did the council finally act?
options: The blocked route forced the council to respond
The women paid for the repairs themselves
The lorry belonged to the council chairman
The road had never been used by farmers
items.explanation: The passage shows that months of complaints were ignored until the lorry blocked the only route, so the council acted only when the road was completely cut off. The other options describe events the passage never mentions.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: The headmaster dismissed the boy's excuse as flimsy, and none of the teachers believed it either. Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word flimsy.
items.explanation: Flimsy describes something easily seen through or lacking substance, so weak and unconvincing is the closest meaning. Long, honest and written describe the form of the excuse, not its lack of credibility.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: She was praised for being thrifty, a habit her brother could never learn because he squandered every allowance he received. Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word thrifty.
items.explanation: Thrifty means careful and economical with money, so its opposite is extravagant, meaning wasteful. Economical and careful are synonyms, while quiet describes manner rather than spending.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Fill the gap. After the final whistle the two captains congratulated ____ for the goals that had decided the match.
items.explanation: Each other is used when exactly two people act on one another, which fits the two captains. One another is preferred for more than two, each others is not English, and themselves would mean each captain congratulated himself.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the second syllable?
items.explanation: The stress in arrange falls on the second syllable, ar-RANGE, while pleasure, gentle and doctor are all stressed on the first syllable.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Which of the following words contains a vowel sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Seat, meat and beat all contain the long vowel sound heard in see, while great contains the different vowel sound heard in gate.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Which of the following words contains a silent letter?
items.explanation: In castle the letter t is not pronounced, so it is silent, whereas table, market and garden have no silent letters.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: The chairman asked the committee not to beat about the bush but to state their decision plainly. What does the expression beat about the bush mean?
items.explanation: To beat about the bush means to avoid saying the important thing directly, which is why the chairman contrasted it with stating the decision plainly. The other options treat the words literally.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Amara and her neighbour planted the same maize seed on the same day and on adjoining plots, yet at harvest Amara gathered far more bags. She had spread manure on her plot while her neighbour applied none. What most likely explains the difference in harvest?
options: Amara added manure that enriched her soil
Amara used a different kind of seed
The neighbour planted a month later
The neighbour sold his maize before harvest
items.explanation: The passage states the seed and the planting day were the same, and the only stated difference was Amara's use of manure, so the manure best explains her larger harvest.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Fill the gap. He has worked in this bank ____ he left secondary school in 2015.
items.explanation: Since is used with a point in time when the action began, here 2015, while for would require a period such as nine years.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Fill the gap. The manager insisted that every applicant ____ the form before the interview.
items.explanation: After verbs such as insist that, English uses the subjunctive, which takes the base form complete for every subject, not completes.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Kwame read the telegram three times, then folded it quietly and walked to the window without saying a word to the family gathered in the room. What does his behaviour most likely suggest?
options: He was angry with the messenger
items.explanation: Reading the message repeatedly and then falling silent while withdrawing from the family suggests the news disturbed him, so troubling news fits best. None of the other options explains his silence.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: The speaker warned that a nation which cannot feed itself cannot truly claim independence, however many flags it raises. What is the speaker's main point?
options: Food self-sufficiency is essential to true independence
Flags are unnecessary for a nation
Independence is impossible for any nation
Farming should be left to foreigners
items.explanation: The warning links the ability to feed the nation with genuine independence, so the main point is that food self-sufficiency is essential. The other options twist or overstate the claim.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Which of the following words begins with a consonant sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Phone, physics and photo all begin with the f sound, while puff begins with the p sound heard in pen.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Fill the gap. This is the ____ interesting book I have read this year.
items.explanation: The superlative is needed because the writer is comparing the book with every other book read that year, and interesting is a long adjective that forms its superlative with most.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: If 4x - 3 = 21, find the value of x.
items.explanation: Adding 3 to both sides gives 4x = 24, so x = 24 divided by 4 = 6. Substituting 6 back gives 24 - 3 = 21, which confirms the answer.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Find the roots of the quadratic equation x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0.
items.explanation: Factorising gives (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0, so the roots are 2 and 3, since 2 times 3 = 6 and 2 + 3 = 5.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Simplify 5^2 multiplied by 5^3, giving the answer as a single number.
items.explanation: When powers of the same base are multiplied the indices are added, so 5^2 times 5^3 = 5^5 = 3125.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Differentiate y = 4x^3 - 2x with respect to x.
items.explanation: Differentiating term by term gives 12x^2 for 4x^3 and minus 2 for 2x, so dy/dx = 12x^2 - 2.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Find the indefinite integral of 6x with respect to x.
items.explanation: Raising the power and dividing by the new power gives 3x^2, and a constant of integration is added, so the integral is 3x^2 + C.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: The arithmetic progression 5, 9, 13 continues in the same way. What is its twentieth term?
items.explanation: The first term is 5 and the common difference is 4, so the twentieth term is 5 + 19 times 4 = 5 + 76 = 81.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: The geometric progression 3, 6, 12 continues in the same way. What is its sixth term?
items.explanation: The common ratio is 2, so the sixth term is 3 times 2^5 = 3 times 32 = 96.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Evaluate the logarithm to base 10 of 10000.
items.explanation: Since 10^4 = 10000, the logarithm to base 10 of 10000 equals 4.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Find the simple interest on a principal of 50000 naira for 2 years at 10 percent per annum.
items.explanation: Simple interest is principal times rate times time, so 50000 times 0.10 times 2 = 10000 naira.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of obtaining an even number?
items.explanation: The even numbers on a die are 2, 4 and 6, giving three favourable outcomes out of six, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Find the mean of the numbers 4, 6, 8 and 10.
items.explanation: The sum is 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 = 28, and dividing by the four numbers gives 28 divided by 4 = 7.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: A trader bought an article for 2000 naira and sold it for 2500 naira. What was the percentage profit?
items.explanation: The profit is 2500 - 2000 = 500 naira, and 500 as a percentage of the cost 2000 is (500/2000) times 100 = 25 percent.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of a regular pentagon?
items.explanation: The sum of the interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n - 2) times 180 degrees, so for a pentagon it is 3 times 180 = 540 degrees.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: If x + y = 12 and x - y = 2, find the value of x.
items.explanation: Adding the two equations gives 2x = 14, so x = 7. Then y = 5, and substituting back gives 7 + 5 = 12 and 7 - 5 = 2.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Simplify the surd expression the square root of 48 plus the square root of 27.
items.explanation: Root 48 = 4 root 3 and root 27 = 3 root 3, so adding gives 4 root 3 + 3 root 3 = 7 root 3.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Mathematics

items.stem: Which definition best describes the subject matter of economics?
options: The study of how governments win elections
The study of how to print more money to end poverty
The study of how scarce resources are allocated to satisfy unlimited human wants
The study of weather and its effect on farming
items.explanation: Economics studies the allocation of scarce resources among competing unlimited wants. The other options describe politics, monetary printing or meteorology rather than the core subject.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: A student gives up a paid part-time job to attend lectures full time. The value of the best alternative she gave up is known as
items.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made, which here is the pay she gave up. Money, fixed and sunk cost refer to different accounting ideas.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: The law of demand states that, other things being equal, when the price of a good rises the quantity demanded will
items.explanation: The law of demand describes an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, so a price rise causes quantity demanded to fall when other factors are unchanged.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: A movement along a given demand curve for a product is caused by a change in
options: the price of a substitute good
the price of the good itself
items.explanation: A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the demand curve, whereas changes in income, taste or substitute prices shift the whole curve to a new position.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: In the ordinary case, the supply curve of a commodity slopes
items.explanation: Producers are generally willing to supply more as price rises, so the supply curve slopes upward from left to right, showing a positive relationship between price and quantity supplied.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: When a 10 percent fall in the price of a good produces a 20 percent rise in the quantity demanded, the demand for the good is
items.explanation: Elasticity is the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price, giving 20 divided by 10 = 2, and any value greater than one means demand is elastic.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: The market for a good is said to be in equilibrium when
options: the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied
the government fixes the price of the good
producers decide to hoard their stock
consumers refuse to buy the good at any price
items.explanation: Equilibrium occurs at the price where the quantity that buyers wish to purchase equals the quantity that sellers wish to sell, so there is no tendency for price to change.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: If a government sets a maximum price for a good below the equilibrium price, the likely result in the short run is
options: no effect on the market at all
items.explanation: At a price below equilibrium quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so a shortage develops. A surplus would occur only if the price were held above equilibrium.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: In the theory of production, the reward for the factor of production called capital is
items.explanation: Capital earns interest, land earns rent, labour earns wages and the entrepreneur earns profit, so interest is the reward for capital.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: Inflation is best described as
options: a one-time rise in the price of a single commodity
a fall in the general price level over time
an increase in the total money supply only
a sustained rise in the general price level
items.explanation: Inflation is a persistent and general rise in prices across the economy, not a one-off change in one good. A general fall in prices is deflation, and money supply growth alone is not inflation.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: To control inflation a central bank may raise the cash reserve ratio it requires banks to hold. The effect of this measure is to
options: reduce the money supply in the economy
increase the amount banks can lend out
lower the rate of interest immediately
items.explanation: A higher cash reserve ratio leaves banks with less lendable funds, so the money supply contracts. The other options describe effects of loosening rather than tightening monetary policy.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: When a trader exchanges a bag of rice for money in the market, money is performing the function of a
items.explanation: Using money to buy and sell goods is its function as a medium of exchange. Storing value, measuring value and settling debts later are separate functions of money.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: A market structure in which there is only one seller of a product that has no close substitutes is called
items.explanation: A monopoly exists where a single firm is the sole seller of a product with no close substitutes, giving it control over price. The other structures all involve more than one seller.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: A production possibility curve shows
options: the money supply of an economy at one point in time
the total profit made by all firms in an economy
the rate at which a population grows each year
the maximum combinations of two goods an economy can produce with given resources
items.explanation: The production possibility curve illustrates the maximum output combinations of two goods possible when all resources are fully and efficiently used, which is why it defines the frontier of production.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: A public good such as street lighting differs from a private good mainly because it is
options: non-excludable, so non-payers cannot be prevented from enjoying it
sold only to the highest bidder
available only to those who pay a fee
items.explanation: Once street lighting is provided, people who did not pay cannot easily be excluded from its benefit, which is the non-excludability that defines a public good. Private goods can exclude non-payers.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Economics

items.stem: A business organisation that is owned, financed and controlled by one person, who bears unlimited liability for its debts, is called a
items.explanation: A sole proprietorship is owned and controlled by one person and, because it has no separate legal personality, the owner's liability for its debts is unlimited.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: In a partnership, a partner who contributes capital to the business but takes no active part in its management is known as a
items.explanation: A dormant or sleeping partner supplies capital but does not share in the running of the business. An active partner manages the firm, while a nominal partner lends only a name.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: The accounting equation states that the resources owned by a business are financed by the owner's capital and by outside liabilities. Which formula correctly represents this equation?
items.explanation: The accounting equation is Assets = Capital + Liabilities, showing that everything the business owns is funded either by the owner or by creditors.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: A trader's business has total assets of 80000 naira and the owner's capital is 50000 naira. Using the accounting equation, what is the amount of the liabilities?
items.explanation: Rearranging the accounting equation gives Liabilities = Assets - Capital = 80000 - 50000 = 30000 naira.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: The rule of double entry bookkeeping requires that for every transaction the accountant should
options: record the transaction only in the cash book
debit the receiver and credit the giver
enter the same amount twice on the debit side
ignore the effect on the owner's capital
items.explanation: Double entry means every transaction has two equal and opposite effects, so the account receiving value is debited and the account giving value is credited.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: A trial balance is prepared at the end of a period mainly in order to
options: calculate the profit made during the period
record all cash payments in one place
check the arithmetical accuracy of the double entry records
show the market value of the business
items.explanation: The trial balance lists debit and credit balances and, if they agree, provides evidence that the double entry postings were arithmetically accurate. Profit is found in the trading account, not the trial balance.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: The working capital of a business is calculated as
items.explanation: Working capital measures the funds available for day to day operations and is current assets minus current liabilities. The other formulas describe different accounting relationships.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: Depreciation of a fixed asset such as machinery is best described as
options: the allocation of the asset's cost over its useful life
the cash set aside to replace the asset
an increase in the market value of the asset
the amount paid to repair the asset
items.explanation: Depreciation spreads the original cost of a fixed asset over the years it is used to earn income, matching cost with revenue rather than recording cash set aside.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: A trade discount is best described as
options: a reduction allowed to a customer for paying his account early
a reduction allowed by a wholesaler to a retailer on the list price
an amount added to the price to cover transport
a tax charged on the sale of goods
items.explanation: A trade discount is a reduction from the list price that a wholesaler grants a retailer, usually because of the size of the order, while a cash discount rewards prompt payment.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: A document sent by a seller to a buyer showing the details and prices of goods supplied on credit is called
items.explanation: An invoice lists the goods sold and their prices and states the amount the buyer owes. A receipt acknowledges payment, while credit and debit notes correct errors or returns.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: When the owner of a business takes goods or cash from the business for personal use, the transaction is called drawings and it will
options: increase the assets of the business
have no effect on the accounts
items.explanation: Drawings reduce the owner's claim on the business, so the drawings account is debited and capital is reduced. They are not business expenses and they reduce assets.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: A trader who buys goods from suppliers on credit records these transactions in the
items.explanation: Credit purchases of goods are recorded in the purchases day book, while the sales day book records credit sales and the cash book records cash transactions.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared in order to
options: calculate the depreciation on bank equipment
reconcile the cash book balance with the bank statement balance
record the salaries paid to bank staff
prepare the balance sheet of the bank
items.explanation: A bank reconciliation statement explains the differences between the balance in the business cash book and the balance shown on the bank statement, tracing items such as unpresented cheques.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: Commerce is broadly divided into two main branches, namely
items.explanation: Commerce is divided into trade, which covers buying and selling, and aids to trade, which include banking, insurance, transport and advertising. The other options are only parts of these branches.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting

items.stem: A cash discount allowed by a seller to a buyer is given mainly to
options: reward the buyer for buying in large quantities
cover the cost of transporting the goods
reduce the list price on all future orders
encourage the buyer to pay the account promptly
items.explanation: A cash discount is offered to encourage early settlement of an account within a stated period, whereas a trade discount rewards a large order and reduces the list price.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Commerce and Accounting
